title: Sparse constrained model discovery identifies isotropic material limit surfaces
summary: The study compares sparse invariant libraries and physically gated mixtures of experts for fitting physically admissible yield and failure surfaces. Across five experimental datasets, richer invariant terms substantially improved the concrete fit (fourfold lower cross-validated error) and a selected TSSA surface combined a maximum-principal-stretch criterion with a cavitation term. The work also identifies substantial model-form uncertainty: hydrostatic tensile strength is weakly constrained, and the proposed quantitative Weibull interpretation is not supported by replicate data.
ai_technology: Sparse differentiable model selection and learned physically gated mixtures of experts fit multiaxial material-failure data subject to admissibility constraints.

evidence.tested: The primary v1 reports synthetic recovery tests, cross-validation and bootstrap analyses on five existing experimental datasets, including foams, PA6, concrete and structural silicone.
evidence.unknown: Hydrostatic tensile strength is weakly constrained; different admissible model classes yield materially different extrapolations. The paper states replicate data do not support its quantitative Weibull interpretation.
